rationale: The assistant correctly told the customer to unplug before turning the drum by hand, obtained the model number, and sensibly escalated to an engineer once the customer said they could not tilt the machine or open it. However it never checked the simplest things (levelling on the wooden floor, where the noise comes from, condenser pump), and leaned heavily and repeatedly on 'worn jockey (idler) pulley or a glazed drive belt' even after the rough drum feel pointed at least as much toward rollers/bearing. No parts were actually recommended and no facts were invented, though the model-number panel was pushed before any inspection and the closing line about it being 'difficult for an engineer as well' is confused.
